solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Against reactionary work by academic from down under

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: a reactionary turns back, so the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
a dean is a senior university academic

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to backward-looking scholarship by a professor from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' is the reversal signal: the word for work is read backwards. OP stands for opus.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes people or things from Australia or New Zealand, colloquially 'down under' to Britons.

clue.text: Bald Cockney lacks any manners

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H sound

parts.note: a bald person lacks any hairs

explanation.surface: A bald Londoner without any social graces.
explanation.walkthrough: What a bald Cockney lacks is ''airs'; Cockneys, from East London, drop H.
explanation.definitionFit: Airs are affected manners, as in putting on airs.

clue.text: Maybe fifth bowler might be thus described?

definitions.meaning: fifth gear is often the highest
a bowler hat is gear worn on top

explanation.surface: A cricket question: is the fifth bowler described like this?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket; it is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Top gear is a vehicle's highest gear, and a hat is clothing worn on the head.

clue.text: Ascendancy of bent copper near end

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman's dominance is nearly over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent copper' looks like a crooked policeman; 'bent' rearranges COPPER NEAR END.
explanation.definitionFit: Preponderance means superiority in weight or power, a dominance.

clue.text: Doctor finding headless fish in swamp

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A doctor discovers a decapitated fish in a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench or swamp is to soak completely with water.

clue.text: Gambling occasionally on fall of cards? It's of some moment

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the deal is how the cards fall to the players

explanation.surface: Betting now and then on how the cards land matters a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A big deal is something important, a matter of moment.

clue.text: Go for Glaswegians, a violent lot

definitions.meaning: in Scots dialect, as spoken in Glasgow

explanation.surface: Telling Glasgow residents to steer clear of a bunch of thugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gang is the Scots verb for walk or go, and in standard English a group of troublemakers.

clue.text: Emergence of a challenger to dictator

indicators.note: one who dictates speaks aloud, so the words are judged by how they are heard

parts.note: a rival is a challenger

explanation.surface: A rival appears to challenge the tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' looks like a tyrant; it is someone dictating aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrival is a coming into view, the appearance of something.

clue.text: Kind of tart whose company's not wanted

definitions.meaning: ... tart is a pie made with the fruit
the third wheel with a courting couple

explanation.surface: A sort of floozy nobody wants to spend time with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' hints at a person; it is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooseberry is a fruit used in tarts, and British idiom for an unwanted third person.

clue.text: Well fed agent hired at end of June

parts.note: a rep (representative) is a sales agent
let means rented out, hired

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word June

explanation.surface: A representative eats well, hired at the close of June.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means full up, satisfied after eating plenty.

clue.text: Conclude working in retirement is hell

parts.note: to conclude something is to infer it

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for working is read backwards

parts.note: on means working, operating

explanation.surface: Deciding to keep working after retiring is pure hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferno is Dante's name for Hell, and generally a blazing, hellish place.

clue.text: Deception that Charlie Chaplin for one was engaged in?

definitions.text: that Charlie Chaplin for one was engaged in?
definitions.meaning: Chaplin was a comedian, so comedy was literally his ...

explanation.surface: Was the great silent comic engaged in trickery?
explanation.definitionFit: Funny business is idiom for underhand dealing, and literally the comedy trade.

clue.text: Enjoyed English cider Jo manufactured at home

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so these letters are assembled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
in means at home

explanation.surface: Jo enjoyed home-brewed English cider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges E + CIDER + JO into REJOICED.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice in something is to take delight in it, so it is a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Letter spelled out change in direction, largely

indicators.note: largely means most of it, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to veer is to change direction

explanation.surface: A letter written out explains a major shift of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the final R of VEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Vee is the name of the letter V written out in full.

clue.text: Burst into tears, nasty head being very loud

indicators.note: burst means broken apart, so the letters are rearranged
head means the first letter of the word nasty

explanation.surface: Someone bursts into tears, a nasty headache being deafening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burst into tears' is a familiar phrase; 'Burst' rearranges INTO TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentorian means extremely loud, after Stentor, the loud-voiced herald in the Iliad.

clue.text: Angry words of one caught in traffic

indicators.note: caught in says the letter for one sits inside the word for traffic

parts.note: traffic as a noun means trade, dealing
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Swearing from someone stuck in a traffic jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, an outburst of furious words.

clue.text: Sailors despondent in the shade

parts.note: the navy is a body of sailors
blue means low, despondent

explanation.surface: Gloomy sailors sitting out of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Navy blue is a particular dark colour, so it is a shade.

clue.text: Grunts of young one on the line

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: an infant is a very young child
RY is the abbreviation for railway, the line

explanation.surface: Noises made by a baby on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grunts' is US slang for foot soldiers, not noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunts are infantry soldiers in American military slang.

clue.text: Displaying curiosity about royal ornament

indicators.note: about says the word for prying goes round the royal letters

parts.note: nosing means prying, displaying curiosity
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone curious about a piece of royal jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose ring is a piece of jewellery worn through the nose, a type of ornament.

clue.text: Crushes a relative

explanation.surface: A relative being squashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps on means treads underfoot, crushing; a stepson is a spouse's son.

clue.text: Jack wants something with milk in it — a shake

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
a cow's udder holds milk

explanation.surface: Jack asks for a milkshake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a shake' looks like the drink Jack wants, but it is a vibration.
explanation.definitionFit: A judder is a violent shaking or vibration.

clue.text: Money companion invested in theatre

indicators.note: invested in says the companion goes inside the word for theatre

parts.note: drama is theatre, the stage
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Cash a partner has put into a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' suggests finance, but here it means placed inside. Companion of Honour is a British order of merit.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro.

clue.text: With new leader, man becomes sad

indicators.note: a new leader means the first letter is swapped for another

parts.note: hombre is Spanish for man, used in English slang

explanation.surface: A man turns gloomy after a change of boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means dark and gloomy in mood, melancholy.

clue.text: Cry in the Bullring, a mess with husband gone

indicators.note: gone means taken away, so the letter for husband is removed

parts.note: being in a hole is being in a mess, so hole means a mess

explanation.surface: A shout from a bullring crowd over a married man's absent chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Olé is the Spanish shout of approval heard at bullfights.

clue.text: Not a Nepali misbehaving — someone else entirely

indicators.note: letters that misbehave won't stay in line, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: That's no unruly Nepali: it's a different person altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, a person who is indeed quite different from a Nepali.

clue.text: Mere daydream, but vicar's drifted off

indicators.note: drifted off means gone away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a reverie is a daydream
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: Just a daydream, but the clergyman nodded off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like 'only'; it is a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake, and Erie is one of the Great Lakes.

clue.text: Examine popular party holding power

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: holding says the word for party wraps round the letter for power

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Scrutinise a well-liked party that holds power.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look over closely, to examine.

clue.text: Gas bubble the retort displays

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A chemist watches gas bubbling in a retort, the glass flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' and 'retort' suggest chemistry; gas here means idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blether is Scots for foolish talk, and to gas is to chatter at length.

clue.text: Outspoken denial from Berlin cardinal

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: nein is German for no

explanation.surface: A German senior churchman's frank refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' looks like a churchman; it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a cardinal number, one used for counting.

clue.text: Charlie nervously creeps by a world infested by trolls?

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: moving nervously means fidgeting, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Charlie creeps anxiously past a land overrun by fairy-tale trolls.
explanation.walkthrough: The trolls are online provocateurs, not creatures under bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet trolls post provocations online, so the online realm is a world they infest.
